title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Media Availability | Wednesday, October 14th | Press Conference
headline: Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) is limited Wednesday but is expected to start Sunday vs. the Bears if all goes to plan; C.J. Henderson sits out but isn't ruled out.
summary: Stefanski opened Bears week with an injury update. Michael Penix Jr. will practice in a limited way, and his reps will depend on how he feels. Stefanski expects him to start Sunday as long as everything goes according to plan, and he declined to give specifics on the rib imaging, saying only that Penix is feeling better. Za'Darius Smith is working back from a neck injury and will be monitored through the week. C.J. Henderson is out of practice today but is getting better and is not ruled out for the game. Stefanski praised Chicago's roster and Dennis Allen's aggressive, multiple defense, and said the team must prepare for all three Bears quarterbacks, not just Caleb Williams. He said the offensive line is working well together under Bill Callahan and that the wide zone core remains intact while some gap concepts are added depending on the opponent. He praised Drake London's work habits and rookie Kendal Daniels for handling a heavy, multi-position workload. He also said Avieon Terrell is improving with more reps.

injuries.detail: Rib injury. Limited in practice, with the number of reps to be determined by how he feels. Expected to start Sunday if all goes to plan. Stefanski said he's feeling better.
Working back from a neck injury. Stefanski will monitor how he feels and responds to treatment over the next few days.
Not practicing Wednesday but getting better. Stefanski is not ruling him out for the game.

signals.claim: Penix will start Sunday against the Bears if his rib injury doesn't set him back this week.
signals.note: He is likely to play, but his limited practice status and the unspecified injury details leave some risk until the end-of-week reports.
signals.quote: As long as everything goes according to plan.

signals.claim: Daniels will continue to handle a large, multi-position workload, including some snaps at end.
signals.note: The coach's trust in a rookie with this much volume and flexibility points to a growing defensive role, mainly relevant for IDP.
signals.quote: Very impressive and don't want to take that for granted.

signals.note: Stefanski described London as a hard-working, focused leader, which supports his standing in the passing game, but he gave no usage details.
signals.quote: Drake's been a pleasure to work with from day one.

signals.claim: Henderson is out of practice Wednesday but could still play Sunday.
signals.note: His availability is uncertain until later practice reports, which affects the secondary's depth.
signals.quote: I'd say out today, but not ruling him out for the game.

signals.claim: Smith's availability for Sunday will depend on how his neck responds to treatment this week.
signals.note: A neck injury with no clear timeline puts the edge rusher's Sunday status in question.

signals.claim: Terrell will keep getting more reps and playing both inside and outside in the secondary.
signals.note: His expanded, versatile role is mainly relevant for IDP.
signals.quote: he's played inside and out for us

topics.detail: Stefanski called Dennis Allen's defense aggressive and varied, able to show pressure and play Cover 3, and said it makes you work for everything in the run and pass game.
The line is working well together under Callahan. The wide zone foundation remains while some gap concepts are added, depending on the opponent and what the players do well.
Stefanski called Caleb Williams tremendous and said the team must prepare for the whole Bears QB room, since two other quarterbacks have started games for Chicago.
With a five-game sample, there is more certainty in scouting, but teams keep changing schemes. Stefanski cautioned against giving players too much film.

title: Ben Johnson on Bears' Week 6 mindset | Press Conference
headline: Montez Sweat is suspended multiple games and Dayo Odeyingbo is likely to miss time, so Austin Booker and Shemar Turner get more edge snaps. Caleb Williams is expected to be a full practice participant Wednesday, but the Week 6 starter is still 'fluid'.
summary: The Bears held a walk-through Wednesday as a planned reset before the bye and turned to Atlanta, whom Johnson called a good team in all three phases. Montez Sweat was suspended for multiple games, and Johnson said he was not aware of any appeal. The coach framed it as 'next man up.' Dayo Odeyingbo left the game hurt. He is not headed to IR but is likely to miss some time, so Austin Booker (rising in snaps and production), the newly promoted Shemar Turner and some inactive linemen could see more work. Tyrique Stevenson is day to day and T.J. Edwards is week to week. Caleb Williams is not 100% and the Week 6 starter is still fluid, but he will be a full participant Wednesday. Johnson said all three QBs are banged up, took the blame for the offense's struggles, and gave no clarity on the QB depth chart behind Williams. D'Andre Swift will not take 50-plus snaps because Chicago believes in a committee backfield, and Rome Odunze's inconsistency was folded into a general 'back to basics' reset. Kyler Gordon is still on PUP and Johnson said all options are open on his activation.

injuries.detail: Suspended for multiple games. Johnson was not aware of any appeal.
Hurt in the game. Not IR-worthy but likely to miss some time, and the duration is unknown.
Day to day.
Week to week.
Not 100%. Expected to be a full participant Wednesday, but the Week 6 starter is still fluid.
On PUP. The team is considering all options on activation within the 21-day window.

signals.note: Another defensive line loss, which deepens the rotation questions.

signals.note: Secondary depth is thin, so his availability matters for the Atlanta passing matchup.

topics.detail: Johnson cited three-and-outs, turnovers and red-zone struggles (1-for-2 last week). He plans to return to the style used in camp and Week 1 and to improve his own play calling.
The unit is banged up, with explosive plays a concern. Johnson stressed stopping Atlanta's elite running game, led by a back who might be an MVP candidate.
The walk-through was a planned reset before the bye. A tight turnaround for the next game after Atlanta (New England) is a consideration in the QB decision.

title: Shane Steichen: Midweek update, Colts vs. Titans
headline: Colts plan to move Josh Downs around to beat third-down doubles and want more explosive runs from Jonathan Taylor. The coach was non-committal on whether newly signed LB Germaine Pratt plays Sunday vs. TEN.
summary: Steichen opened by stressing the importance of a home division game against the Titans. He said Germaine Pratt, signed to the practice squad, will be brought up to speed this week, with no promise he plays Sunday. He framed the signing as adding veteran presence to a young linebacker room. He said another veteran signing was not injury related, and that Will Mallory is still being evaluated this week. On the offense, he said defenses are doubling Josh Downs on third down, so the Colts must move him around and find the single-coverage looks. He said target distribution flips from week to week and he isn't worried about receivers other than Tyler Warren. He said Jonathan Taylor needs scheme answers to different fronts and cleaner execution, and the run game has lacked the chunk plays it had last year. Red-zone efficiency and takeaways/ball security were the main areas for improvement, and he described the team's identity as fast, physical and disciplined.

injuries.detail: Still being evaluated this week; no specifics given.
Asked about his knee injury, Steichen said only that he is doing better.

signals.claim: Will be moved around the formation more to get him open against third-down double coverage.
signals.note: Defenses are focused on him, but the Colts plan to scheme him free, which supports his target floor.
signals.quote: they're doubling him on third down a few times

signals.claim: Colts will adjust schematically to different defensive fronts to try to create explosive runs for Taylor.
signals.note: Taylor has had no chunk plays in the run game this year, so efficiency depends on the scheme and execution fixes working.
signals.quote: We haven't had those in the run game.

signals.claim: Target volume will vary week to week, and Warren may not have the biggest game every week.
signals.note: Warren is producing, but the coach said the target split between him and others flips week to week.
signals.quote: Tyler might have ten catches and maybe Josh has three.

signals.claim: Mallory's status will be evaluated this week before a decision on Sunday.
signals.note: Tight end depth is uncertain, so check his practice participation.
signals.quote: we're still evaluating Mallory this week and see where it goes.

signals.claim: Brown was signed as a veteran contributor, not because of injuries at tight end.
signals.note: Tight end depth chart could shift, though the coach played down any link to injuries. The identification of Brown from the garbled question is moderately confident.
signals.quote: He's a veteran player that can help us.

topics.detail: Pratt was signed to the practice squad as a veteran presence for a young linebacker room. The Colts will see where he is this week, and there is no guarantee he plays Sunday.
Steichen cited a fast-tempo try at the goal line, a failed goal-line run and a missed third-down conversion. He said the plan needs to be dialed in and executed at a high level.
Takeaways and taking care of the football are the top priority and must be practiced constantly.
Tennessee has Pro Bowl returner Dye (DK), so coverage lanes on kicks and punts matter. Indy also wants explosive returns to flip the field.
Asked whether a recently added receiver (name unclear in the captions) could play, he said only that they would see how the week goes.
He described the identity as fast, physical and disciplined and said he sees no lack of effort. He said execution needs to be better and called player self-criticism accountability.

title: Coen on "Next Man Up" Mentality, Red Zone Execution & WR Marvin Harrison Jr. | Press Conference
headline: Tackle out for a game after a procedure, Eric Murray (limited) and Trevor Lawrence's improving pocket play are the fantasy watch items for the Houston game.
summary: Coen said the injured tackle will have a procedure after the team returns and that there is no clear timeline yet, so they will take it day by day. He has confidence in Walker Little and Cole Van Lanen to replace him, with a next-man-up mindset. On Houston, he expects a physical test: their run defense is strong, they play more man coverage at times, and their record doesn't change how he views them. He praised C.J. Stroud for getting the ball out on time, scrambling more, and making contested-catch throws with his receivers. Coen said the offense must execute better in the red zone, admitted some self-inflicted mistakes and play-call issues, and said the offense held a candid meeting on Monday. He praised Trevor Lawrence's improved movement in the pocket and throwing on the run, and said the fourth-down touchdown to Parker Washington came from a slot fade. Eric Murray has not been able to do much since last week, and Coen will see how he moves today and tomorrow. Josh Cameron has been impressive on special teams and as a blocker. Kaevon Merriweather was elevated to help special teams, with a long snapper and the Ross timeline factored in.

injuries.detail: Has not done much since last week; the team will evaluate his movement today and tomorrow before deciding on his status.

signals.claim: Pocket movement and throwing on the run have improved, which the coach credits to the team challenging him in that area.
signals.note: Improved mobility and off-platform throwing can add rushing and big-play upside in the passing game.
signals.quote: He's extremely good when throwing to his left on the move.

signals.note: Shows he is trusted in critical situations, which supports red-zone and third-down target value.
signals.quote: Got Parker isolated in the slot on a slot fade.

signals.note: A strong showing in a bigger role suggests he is trusted in the defensive back end.
signals.quote: Antonio really, really stepped up last week and had one of his best games.

signals.note: His availability against his former team is uncertain and could shift the secondary rotation.

signals.claim: Continues to play a big role on special teams and as a blocker, and is a versatile contributor.
signals.note: Special-teams and blocking roles can add snaps and offensive opportunities for a rookie.

signals.note: This is a depth move, not a fantasy-relevant role change, unless his snaps grow.
signals.quote: Bringing Kayvon up gave us a good chance.

topics.detail: Coen said the offense must execute better in the red area, owns some of the play-calling issues, and noted the Monday meeting cleared up the problems.
Coen praised the defensive play-calling, including pressure disguises and mixing up rushers, and said the defense kept the team in the game in the second half.
Coen is pleased with the tight end group's versatility across personnel packages, with 11 and 12 personnel giving flexibility.
Coen said the team's 10-day stay in the area has been positive for routine and rhythm, but he does not believe it changes the outcome on Sunday.

title: Andy Reid on Chargers: 'They Play Hard and They're Well Coached' | Press Conference 10/14
headline: Rashee Rice is the only player not practicing Wednesday, Tyquan Thornton's role is open after an apparent injury, and Xavier Worthy is among the receivers expected to absorb it.
summary: Reid said Rashee Rice is the only player who won't do anything at Wednesday's practice, and everyone else is scheduled to do something. A tackle named Josh (not clearly identifiable from the roster) is back at practice on a limited basis, and Reid will ease him in after back trouble. Reid said another injured player, whose name was lost in the captions, has a hamstring issue that could take a week or two, though he's feeling good and eager to return. Reid called the Chargers a good, well-coached team that plays hard despite its record and injuries, and said it's largely the group that beat up on KC last year. After the early bye, Reid said the self-scouting found nothing new except that short-yardage offense must improve. On Tyquan Thornton, who was having a very good year and is now out, Reid said another player will get the opportunity and that he trusts all the receivers, naming Xavier Worthy, who has had a couple of good catches recently. He said the fourth and fifth receivers get plenty of practice reps and rotate in, and that he and Patrick Mahomes are comfortable with that group. Reid had not yet considered what happens with Kahlil Benson when Josh returns to the lineup.

title: Sean McVay breaks down special teams changes, takeaways from Bills matchup, preparing for Week 6 & more
headline: Alaric Jackson is suspended two games (appealing), so David Quessenberry starts at LT. Kyren Williams keeps a real receiving role, and Davante Adams is expected to keep improving.
summary: McVay opened by confirming the Rams released their kicker and signed a replacement, saying the team needs better production there. He said special teams cost them a chance to win the Monday game against Buffalo but weren't the only reason they lost. Left tackle Alaric Jackson was suspended two games after the game; McVay said he learned of it that morning, that Jackson will appeal, and that he wants to gather the full facts before saying more. Quessenberry will take Jackson's spot. McVay also said a player's practice clock will not be started this week; the transcript doesn't make clear who he meant. He called the penalty count (42 in five games, including four pre-snap false starts from four different players) uncharacteristic and expects it to be a blip. He praised Matthew Stafford's performance and said Kyren Williams' receiving volume is both a product of the defense and a deliberate role. He expects Davante Adams to keep improving after missing much of training camp. McVay took the blame for the late-game decision that led to the missed overtime field goal and said he has no plans to change special teams coordinators. The team came out of the game healthy, and the offense has been strong in two-minute situations in recent weeks.

injuries.detail: Has played three games after missing much of training camp. McVay said he came out of the Bills game feeling good and expects him to keep improving.

signals.note: The starting left tackle is out for at least two games, which could weaken pass protection and run blocking up front.

signals.note: He steps into a starting role at left tackle for the next two games.

signals.note: He had six more catches, is tied for the NFL lead in RB receptions, and McVay called his role a mix of design and checkdowns, which gives him PPR value.
signals.quote: he's done a great job in that phase of continuing to improve

signals.note: He has played only three games and is trending up, so his production could grow.
signals.quote: And he's only going to continue to get better.

signals.note: McVay praised his progressions and two-minute operation, which supports the passing volume and an offense that does well in late-game situations.

topics.detail: The Rams released their kicker and signed a veteran who was a perfect 11 for 11 on field goals and 10 for 10 on extra points for Indianapolis last year. They chose game experience over a kicking competition.

McVay said special teams cost them a chance to win the Buffalo game: a first-kickoff coverage mistake, plus a field goal protection breakdown against Rousseau. He expressed confidence in coordinator Bubba Ventrone and said no coaching changes are coming.
The Rams have 42 penalties in five games, including four false starts from four different players. McVay called the pre-snap penalties out of character and expects the problem to fade.

McVay said the defense played well enough to win. They forced two turnovers, but Buffalo got screens and lost-rush-integrity plays. The run game was harder because Buffalo committed extra defenders to the front, though the offense scored on three touchdown drives.

The team came out of the Monday game fairly healthy with only typical bumps and bruises. McVay said a player's practice clock will not be started this week; the transcript does not make clear who he meant.

McVay said the offense has executed well in two-minute situations in recent weeks (Denver, Philadelphia, Buffalo). He credited Stafford's handling of the two-minute operation and the team's late touchdown drives.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Khalil Mack's Mentorship of Akheem Mesidor
headline: Chargers are winless and banged up (Mack, Alt, Derwin James, Donte Jackson and others missed practice), and Harbaugh gave no explanation for Omarion Hampton's third straight week of reduced snaps, calling the backfield a three-man group.
summary: Harbaugh opened with the injury report: KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Joe Alt, Derwin James, Donte Jackson, Rodney Shelley and Khalil Mack did not practice, and one other name was garbled in the captions. He said Mack is working to get back, and that Cole (likely Cole Strange) looks ready to return and bring energy. The team signed a practice-squad receiver, Luke Grimm, after a workout, and Harbaugh said the receiver room is set this week. He said the team badly wants its first win and compared it to getting the first olive out of a packed jar. Pressed repeatedly on Omarion Hampton's declining carries and snaps, he praised Hampton's all-around play, spoke well of Kimani Vidal and Keaton Mitchell, and said he does not track touch counts. He said Justin Herbert keeps responding well to adversity, and that Herbert's running was effective last week. He praised Akheem Mesidor and Khalil Mack's mentorship, and said the team's leaders have not been deflated by the winless start. On the Chiefs, he respected Kenneth Walker and Patrick Mahomes but gave no scheme specifics.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 14, 2026
headline: Landon Dickerson's activation from IR/PUP is still undecided and may be announced later Wednesday, while Eli Stowers' status stays vague. Sirianni says the offense is struggling in short yardage, and the team is 'lost more than we've won'.
summary: Sirianni opened by saying Jalen Hurts' rushing depends on the week's game plan, noting that Hurts can hurt defenses as a passer, on designed QB runs, and on scrambles. He was non-committal about activating Landon Dickerson, saying more information would come later in the day. He praised Dickerson's work ethic and the care he has taken of his body, but declined to say whether Dickerson would return at left guard, saying there is plenty of time to decide. He also dodged why Eli Stowers wasn't activated when he first became eligible, saying every player's timetable is different and that he doesn't get into injury details. He admitted the offense has not executed or designed plays well enough in short yardage and called it an area for improvement. He said everything is on the table regarding Sean Mannion (or the play-caller) possibly moving from the booth to the field, and that the team has lost more than it has won. For Carolina, he praised Bryce Young's quick release, fast processing, and ability to keep his eyes downfield when scrambling, and singled out two defenders (#95 and #7) as standouts. He also said Jonathan Bernard is working hard to return from a setback and that expectations for him haven't changed.

injuries.detail: Activation decision pending; Sirianni said information would come later Wednesday and that Dickerson is working hard and determined to return.
Was eligible to come off the list last week but wasn't activated; Sirianni gave no reason and said timetables differ.

signals.claim: Dickerson may be activated, with an announcement later Wednesday.
signals.note: A Dickerson return would help the shaky offensive line, which affects Hurts, Barkley, and the run game, but his role and timing remain unclear.
signals.quote: you guys will get some of that information a little later today.

signals.note: Sirianni wouldn't commit to Dickerson stepping back in at left guard, saying the current linemen are doing a good job.

signals.claim: Hurts' QB runs will depend on the defense and game plan, with no commitment to more rushing.
signals.note: There is no guarantee of increased rushing volume for Hurts, so don't count on a rushing boost.
signals.quote: Sometimes it doesn't.

signals.note: Stowers' return timing is unknown and the coach declined to explain why he wasn't activated last week.
signals.quote: everybody's timetable is a little bit different.

topics.detail: Sirianni acknowledged the team is not executing or designing short-yardage plays well enough and said it's an area of improvement. He said fourth-down decisions weigh analytics along with many other factors.
Asked about moving the play-caller from the booth to the field, he said everything is on the table and the team will turn over every stone to win.

Sirianni praised Bryce Young's quick release, processing, and ability to keep his eyes downfield when extending plays, and said Philadelphia needs to keep him in the pocket. He also highlighted Carolina's #95 and #7 on defense and the team's flying-around style.
He said the Eagles have lost more than they've won and haven't done a good enough job. He praised Jordan Mailata as a stabilizing captain on a shuffling offensive line.
Bernard has not been fully healthy since the start of camp and had a setback, but Sirianni said expectations haven't changed and he looks forward to his return.

title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald Gives Final Updates Ahead Of Week 6 at Broncos
headline: Charbonnet is out at Denver and Drake Thomas is also out (Tyrice Knight steps in). Jaxon Smith-Njigba is good to go on the short week, and Irvin Charles is off IR with a small offensive role possible.
summary: Macdonald said the team's focus after recent losses is on "doubling down" on its process. He framed that as attacking problems, finding solutions and having each other's backs, and called it a lesson for the newer players. Drake Thomas will not be available for the Broncos game, though Macdonald praised his toughness for finishing last week's game and could not say whether the absence is only a one-week issue. Tyrice Knight will step in, and the coach expressed confidence in him with no change in the defensive standard. Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Leonard Williams both made it through the short week and are ready to play. Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet looks great but will not play in this game, and he noted that the team is not yet nine months out from the knee injury. Irvin Charles was brought off IR, and Macdonald called him a heck of a special teams player who could also help on offense in a limited way, with no timetable for his debut. He also praised Denver's quarterback, Bo Nix, and receiver Jaylen Waddle, who has joined Denver's offense, but said Seattle has little recent crossover tape.

title: Todd Bowles on Bucky Irving: ‘Determined to Win’ | Press Conference
headline: Baker Mayfield still hasn't thrown and has no timeline, so rookie Jalon Daniels may start again; Bucky Irving and the run game are the focus, and Sean Tucker has a quad issue.
summary: Bowles said there is no update on Baker Mayfield. He is getting better, but he had not thrown yet and the team will see how he looks after throwing that afternoon. Bowles would not say whether Mayfield could practice Wednesday through Friday until he throws, and said that if Mayfield isn't 100%, he doesn't need to play. Bowles praised Jalon Daniels for how he commands the huddle and the offense after two starts. He said the game has slowed down for him mentally and that he doesn't look like a rookie. He called the running game a 'success formula' and wants to keep building it each week. He credited Bucky Irving's determination and hunger for a career day. Sean Tucker was working with a trainer because of a quad injury, and his status will be clearer Friday. In the secondary, Tykee Smith took over some of Antoine Winfield Jr.'s duties and is the only experienced safety available right now. Bowles also praised Keionte Scott and A'Shawn Robinson, and spent time on how tough Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers' front and tight ends are to face.

topics.detail: Bowles called Rodgers a nightmare to game plan against because of his intelligence, accuracy and ability to read the defense before the snap.

The Steelers' front is smart and fundamentally sound, so Tampa Bay's offensive line will have to be technically sharp. Bowles also said the Steelers' two tight ends both block and run well, and he praised Pittsburgh's running back for his rushing and receiving.
Bowles said tackling can still be improved during the season through drills with dummies and wrapping up in padded practices.
Asked about going for two when down eight, Bowles said it depends on the game situation. He said criticism of coaches comes with the job and that he leans on experienced people.
Bowles said the team's nickel spot has worked well for young players because they have the mindset and knowledge to cover for each other.
